SAS INTCK(interval, start, end <, method>)

Source: R/doc_functions.R
sas_f_intck.Rd

Number of interval boundaries between two dates. See the SAS documentation (Functions and CALL Routines).

Arguments

interval

Character interval name such as 'DAY', 'WEEK', 'MONTH', 'QTR', 'YEAR', 'DTDAY', 'HOUR'; may include a multiplier and shift index (e.g. 'MONTH2.2').

from

Starting date, time or datetime value (must match the interval type).

to

Ending date, time or datetime value.

method

Optional counting method: 'DISCRETE' (default, 'D') counts interval boundaries crossed; 'CONTINUOUS' ('C') counts complete intervals measured from from.

.at

Internal: source position c(line, column) used in log NOTEs.

Value

A vector with one result per element (arguments are recycled), as the SAS function returns per observation.

Differences from R

SAS dates count days and SAS datetimes count seconds from 1960-01-01; R's Date and POSIXct start at 1970-01-01.

See also

Other datetime functions: sas_f_datdif(), sas_f_date(), sas_f_datejul(), sas_f_datepart(), sas_f_datetime(), sas_f_day(), sas_f_dhms(), sas_f_hms(), sas_f_hour(), sas_f_intnx(), sas_f_juldate(), sas_f_juldate7(), sas_f_mdy(), sas_f_minute(), sas_f_month(), sas_f_qtr(), sas_f_second(), sas_f_time(), sas_f_timepart(), sas_f_today(), sas_f_week(), sas_f_weekday(), sas_f_year(), sas_f_yrdif()

Examples

# INTCK: each call is explained above it and followed by its result
# (dates are SAS day counts from 1960-01-01)

# Discrete method (default): one month boundary between 31 Jan and 1 Feb 2020.
sas_f_intck("month", 21945, 21946)  # intck('month','31JAN2020'd,'01FEB2020'd) = 1
#> [1] 1

# Continuous method 'c': less than a full month between 31 Jan and 1 Feb 2020,
# so 0.
sas_f_intck("month", 21945, 21946, "c")  # intck('month','31JAN2020'd,'01FEB2020'd,'c') = 0
#> [1] 0

# One year boundary between 31 Dec 2019 and 1 Jan 2020.
sas_f_intck("year", 21914, 21915)  # intck('year','31DEC2019'd,'01JAN2020'd) = 1
#> [1] 1

# A start after the end counts boundaries backwards: -2 months.
sas_f_intck("month", 21975, 21915)  # intck('month','01MAR2020'd,'01JAN2020'd) = -2
#> [1] -2
